messages.author: 3f331fa86d94e570
messages.subject: Correlated random effects
parts:
Dear all,

Is there a way to fir a model in which a vector corresponding to two random effects u = [a; m] has the following covariance structure: u ~ N(0, G (x) A) using INLA? Here (x) represents the Kronecker product, and it is assumed that G ~ Inverse Wishart. Also, matrix A is known. I looked through the documentation, but couldn't find anything related, but if there is already a thread related to this topic feel free to delete this one.

Kind regards,

Napo

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Correlated random effects
parts:
I don't know if there is any implementation that is made for this.

However, the general implementations "generic0" and "rgeneric" allows any user defined Gaussian (with sparse precision matrix), as a model component.

See 
>>> inla.doc("generic") 
for documentation on these.

Kind regards,
Haakon Bakka

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Correlated random effects
parts:
For completeness:
The Wishart part of the model (Wishart for the precision = Inverse
Wishart for the covariance) is available up to dimension 5:
http://www.math.ntnu.no/inla/r-inla.org/doc/latent/iid123d.pdf
Kronecker product models are implemented using the "group" feature
(the group and control.group arguments to f() models), but only for a
limited range of models, which (according to ?control.group) does not
include generic0,
so the rgeneric approach is needed for this particular Kronecker
product model, but not for some others (e.g. ar1; see ?control.group
for the list).

Finn
